summary.text: A 24-year-old male professional soccer player received a direct blow to the chest from an opponent’s knee during a match and felt severe, throbbing and shooting lower rib cage pain, 8/10 on a visual analog scale and aggravated by dorsal and lateral decubitus. Two weeks of conservative treatment by the team physiotherapist gave no improvement. He visited a sports clinic after about three weeks of pain and reported he could not sleep well because of it.

Examination reproduced the pain with rib pressure, palpation of the costal rim of the 9th and 10th ribs, the Valsalva manoeuvre and sit-up tests. The hooking manoeuvre was positive, traction on the ribs caused pain and no deformity or skin change was seen. Blood pressure was 110/60 mm hg with pulse 58 beats/min. Chest x-ray showed no signs of rib fracture, and the player was diagnosed with Cyriax syndrome.

Conservative therapy with tramadol, acetaminophen and diclofenac was given for one week and he was encouraged to avoid sport, but he returned two weeks later with the same symptoms. Two series of local 1% lidocaine infiltrations were given, then light rehabilitation exercises over one month. Pain decreased gradually and he resumed professional activity after three months.
